en: Archimedes famously claimed he could move the Earth if given a lever long enough and a fulcrum to rest on.
Gecko feet have millions of tiny hairs that increase friction, allowing the lizard to climb smooth glass walls without falling.
Sagittarius A is the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy with gravity so strong not even light escapes.
The Japanese SCMaglev train uses powerful superconducting magnets to levitate above the tracks, eliminating friction and allowing speeds over 600 kilometers per hour.
Benjamin Franklin famously flew a silk kite with a metal key during a thunderstorm to prove that lightning is a form of electricity.
The transatlantic MAREA submarine cable uses total internal reflection to bounce light signals through thin glass threads, transmitting internet data at the speed of light.
The sperm whale produces the loudest biological sound on Earth, using powerful clicks reaching 230 decibels to echolocate prey in the deep ocean.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts thermal energy from underground hot springs into electricity by using steam to spin large turbines.
The sunflower plant converts radiant energy from the sun into chemical energy stored in its seeds and leaves for later growth.
The Ferris wheel, invented by George Washington Gale Ferris Jr., uses the wheel and axle simple machine to lift passengers high into the air.
The streamlined body of a mako shark reduces fluid friction, allowing it to swim through water at speeds up to 70 kilometers per hour.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa remains standing despite its tilt because its center of gravity still falls directly within its wide base.
